html:
SMTO-HTTP-0025 — The selected Gateway can't make web requests

GUID: 7366c41f-fe83-4dc4-a9b7-5a1f2b0887b7
Slug: http-unavailable
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO sends web service requests through a Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to reach other computers and services). No connected Gateway that supports this is selected, so nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and check that at least one Gateway is listed and its Status shows Connected. SMTO needs a connected Gateway to send any web request.
  2. If that Gateway shows Update available, expand it and select its Update button once its running tasks are finished. Older Gateways may not offer web requests; updating stops the Gateway's running tasks, so wait for them first.
  3. Choose that Gateway for your next message and ask for the web request as a new task. Leave a task that already started on its original Gateway. A task keeps the Gateway it started with, so the request has to run as new work on the Gateway that supports it.

What success looks like

  • The new task sends the web request and SMTO shows the service's reply.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Gateway's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't move an already running or saved task to another Gateway without checking with them.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Native HTTP is unavailable in this context: no Gateway route is configured, the Gateway client lacks HTTP support, or the selected Gateway does not advertise (or has unknown) http_request support.

What this means

  • Capability availability reported that the current context cannot use native HTTP on its selected Gateway. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Capability availability reported that the current context cannot use native HTTP on its selected Gateway.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the advertised availability reason and Gateway readiness rather than guessing the destination API failed.

How to fix it

  • skills/_shared/availability.http reports unavailable when the context has no gateway_client or Gateway route (gateway_url, gateway_endpoints or gateway_id), the client lacks http_request, or the run's Gateway capability snapshot marks http_request unsupported or UNKNOWN. Connect or update a Gateway that advertises http_request (refresh Gateway metadata if UNKNOWN) and start new work on it; do not retarget a saved run.
  • Select a connected Gateway that advertises native HTTP support.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The current context advertises native HTTP availability on the intended Gateway.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
